data.question_title:
Our body is a wondrous mechanism and when subjected to unusual stress over a period of time, it adapts itself to deal more effectively with that stress. So when you exert your muscles against resistance, they are forced to adapt and deal with this extraordinary workload. This is the principal of weight training. Strands of muscle fibers become thicker and stronger in response to the demands placed on them.

One of the great merits of weight training is the strength of your heart. During weight training, your heart is forced to beat faster and stronger in order to pump sufficient blood to the muscles being worked. In time, your heart like your body, will adapt to the extra work load by becoming stronger and more efficient Since your body needs a given amount of blood to perform its daily tasks your heart will now need fewer beats to pump the same quantity of blood. Sounds good? There’s more your entire circulatory system is given a thorough workout every time you exercise, which increases its overall efficiency even the neural parts from your brain’s command centers to each individual muscle become more effective, enabling easier recruitment of muscle fibers for carrying out physical tasks. In essence, your body becomes a well-oiled and finely tuned piece of machinery, whirring along without any breakdown In today’s stress filled world, you need all the help you can get.
